text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-A committee of the ruling Labour Party wants to impose tighter controls on Norway's electricity industry. The committee says the market forces have created a shortage of power and higher prices.
-Norwegian shipyards had higher order volumes in 1996 than in 1995. However, profits and equity capital are still low in most shipyards.
-According to Deutsche Bank Research, Norwegian interest rates will probably fall even further if Norwegian authorities do not change the fiscal policy.
-Experts say 100,000 Norwegians are snoring heavily in their sleep.
-A lack of oil rigs in the North Sea is delaying plans to start new drilling projects. The current market situation means that the rig companies get paid up to $120,000-$150,000 per day.
-OECD president Donald Johnston says Norway's economy is among the strongest in the group. Today Johnston will discuss the world economy as well as OECD issues with Norwegian officials.
